rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration with well-established encoders (scgpt and resnet50) and aggregation/fusion methods. This clarifies whether multimodal approaches with standard components can achieve strong performance, providing foundational insights into the importance of encoder choices and fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves 0.4709 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to avgpool aggregation (while keeping RNA/image encoders, profile setting, and fusion type identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. This is a low-risk, high-informative change that addresses a key design choice with minimal parameter shifts.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation (config_002) outperforms transformer aggregation (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to pca_n2000 (a simpler representation) while using avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (a different fusion strategy) can further improve performance. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder complexity and fusion method, both critical design choices, while building on the promising avgpool aggregation from config_002.

Existing evidence shows config_006 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation and concat fusion (vs avgpool/weighted) could improve performance, isolating the impact of these critical design choices. It builds on the top-performing configuration while exploring key architectural variations under the limited budget.

Existing evidence shows that config_006 (pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion identical. It isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, to determine if ViT improves performance over ResNet50 in this context. This is a logical extension of the top-performing configuration and reduces uncertainty about a key component.

Existing evidence shows that config_006 (pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method constant) improves performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation strategy, a key design choice, and builds on the promising combination of pca_n2000 RNA and weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows that config_006 (pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder while keeping other components (pca_n2000 RNA, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) consistent. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice is a critical factor, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_006) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to scvi_n200 RNA encoder and avgpool aggregation while keeping resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion reduces performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder and aggregation choices. It balances exploitation of strong performers with exploration of critical design factors.

Existing evidence shows that config_045 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests changing the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping other components (scvi_n200, avgpool, weighted) consistent, isolating the effect of the image encoder. This is critical to determine if a more advanced vision transformer (ViT) improves performance, despite the risk of overfitting, as it directly addresses a key design choice with high uncertainty.

The existing evidence shows that config_026 (singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether removing aggregation (None) while keeping other parameters the same affects performance, isolating the impact of aggregation choice. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses uncertainty about the importance of aggregation methods in this high-performing configuration.
